narrative:
On October 13, 2026, the Karnataka High Court recorded an overall hearing rate of 31.2%, taking up 928 out of 2,979 scheduled matters across 52 judges. This represents a noticeable drop in judicial activity compared to recent sessions, including October 12 (45.7% heard out of 2,965), October 9 (42.6% of 2,701), and October 8 (46.1% of 3,021).

Judicial efficiency varied significantly across court halls. S. Vishwajith Shetty demonstrated strong output in Hall 21, taking up 81.6% of scheduled cases (84 of 103), while G. Basavaraja achieved a 74.1% hearing rate in Hall 32 (43 of 58). D. K. Singh and H. Shanthi Bhushan also maintained high productivity in Hall 4, hearing 90.9% of matters on their supplementary list and 69.8% on their primary list. Conversely, several halls logged little to no output, including Hall 30 under S. Rachaiah, where none of the 160 listed cases were heard, and Hall 16 under R. Nataraj, which converted just 7 of 116 scheduled matters (6.0%).

Across procedural stages, matters listed for Orders recorded the highest conversion at 37.1% (402 of 1,083 heard), followed by Preliminary Hearings at 29.8% (93 of 312) and Admission at 26.8% (179 of 669). Final Hearings saw a lower conversion rate of 18.5% (99 of 535), declining from 30.4% on the prior day. Regarding case categories, Criminal Appeals (CRL.A) led clearance rates at 64.0% (57 of 89 heard), alongside Commercial Appeals (COMAP) at 60.9% (14 of 23). In contrast, Writ Petitions (WP)—comprising the largest bulk with 1,318 listed cases—saw a conversion rate of 25.8% (340 heard), down from 39.5% on October 12, while Regular Second Appeals (RSA) experienced near-total stagnation with only 1 of 127 listed cases heard (0.8%).
